messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — starting onboarding for Eris-6B (https://huggingface.co/eris/eris-6b). Upstream readme calls out CC-BY-NC-4.0 and an extra 'no commercial hosting' note. Before we add to hosted catalog or make embeddings available, need legal + eng-ml check. Also planning 8-bit and 4-bit quant experiments. Any immediate red flags? :thinking_face:

licensebot: Automated scan result: Detected license = CC-BY-NC-4.0. Flags: commercial use restricted; redistribution allowed with attribution; derivative works allowed but must be non-commercial. See https://huggingface.co/eris/eris-6b/blob/main/LICENSE

maria: @alex can you paste the excerpt? If it's NC then offering inference via our paid hosted API would be commercial use and likely not allowed. Also shipping quantized weights to customers = redistribution. Need legal intake.

sam: For Private deployments customers run it themselves, but if we provide a container with weights or export quantized binaries we are redistributing. For Dedicated (we host on reserved infra) running inference on behalf of a paying customer seems commercial too. (reaction :eyes:)

jordan: Quick numbers from our eval run (internal eval set, short prompts). Baseline fp16 vs quant: 
```
Eris-6B fp16 baseline
ROUGE-L: 38.6
BLEU: 12.3

8-bit (nf4)
ROUGE-L: 38.2 (-0.4)
BLEU: 12.1 (-0.2)

4-bit (q4_k)
ROUGE-L: 36.5 (-2.1)
BLEU: 11.0 (-1.3)
```
4-bit shows a non-trivial quality regression on our task. We should avoid exposing 4-bit weights externally until we confirm fidelity.

li: Small nuance: legal vs technical — hosting vs redistribution. Running inference (hosted API) is a commercial offering; but if customers bring their own license and host in their VPC (Private on-prem), that might be OK. Still risky to supply derivatives.

maria: Confirming: CC-BY-NC's 'non-commercial' term is broad. Offering paid API or charging for access is commercial. Even Dedicated with contractual fees is commercial. For Private where customer self-hosts we still cannot distribute modified weights. We should not ship quantized binaries or container images containing weights without an upstream commercial license. I'll open a legal intake ticket.

alex: Plan proposal:
1) Do NOT add Eris-6B to hosted catalog or enable embeddings for customers yet.
2) Continue internal evals (no exports of weights outside sandboxed infra).
3) Run more 8-bit benches and compare latency/cost delta; avoid 4-bit public builds for now.
4) Reach out to upstream for commercial licensing / dual-license option.
5) Add a blocking flag to model-onboarding checklist.

sam: I'll mark the model 'license: NC - block hosted' in the onboarding sheet and remove any automated deploy rules. Also will ensure our quant pipeline won't write artifacts to shared S3 buckets.

maria: Filed legal intake: LIC-345 — reaching out to upstream counsel. Will update here when we have a permission path. :+1:

alex: Thanks all. If upstream allows commercial hosting we can revisit; until then keep experiments internal only. :thumbsup:
